title: Determination of comprehensive cannabinoid and terpene profiles after controlled inhalation of cannabis flowers – a pilot project to acquire kinetic data and to assess their potential as innovative markers in forensic toxicological routine
summary:
Cannabis laws in Germany have become more liberal —but questions about cannabis have become more complicated. Current standard tests cannot adequately address all of these questions. Presently, within the scope of a forensic toxicological examination, the psychoactive compound THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) and its metabolites are detected in blood. In this research project, participants will inhale cannabis and blood samples will be collected. In addition to THC, other substances in blood will be tested. These substances could provide further information on whether someone is currently under the influence, what type of cannabis was administered (for example, if the use of medicinal cannabis was reported), and how the cannabis was administered (for example, by smoking a “joint” or using a vaporizer). 
It is also particularly important to reliably identify drivers under the influence of cannabis and to assess their ability to drive safely, for example during a traffic stop by the police. After consuming cannabis, participants will therefore be asked to perform simple physical tests, known as “standardised field sobriety tests” (SFST). These tests assess vision, motor skills, balance, coordination, and ability to estimate time. The aim is to investigate whether these tests are suitable for detecting impairments in the aforementioned performance domains under the influence of cannabis. In addition, saliva tests similar to those that might be used during a police traffic stop will be conducted on several occassions.
Furthermore, it is of interest to examine how cannabis can affect internal regulatory systems (stress, endocannabinoids).
conditions: No specific disease or health issue is being studied. The primary focus is on determining the kinetic profiles of THC and other compounds in the cannabis plant.

interventions.name: Six participants will be divided into two groups, with each group participating on a different day, resulting in a total of four study days. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
healthy, participants, capable of giving consent; prior experience with cannabis; a two-week period of abstinence from cannabis prior to the study days
Exclusion criteria:
severe (treatment-requiring) cardiovascular or respiratory diseases, liver or kidney diseases, diabetes mellitus, severe (treatment-requiring) mental and/or neurological disorders, inner ear disorders, vertigo, cannabis abuse, cannabis dependence, adverse events requiring clinical treatment due to a history of cannabis intoxication, current or past alcohol/drug abuse, alcohol and drug dependence, pregnancy and breastfeeding, blood donation within last 30 days, individuals unable to give informed consent, very high frequency of cannabis use, positive result in the alcohol and/or drug screening test (excluding cannabis) on the study day; regular use of products containing cannabinoids, such as non-psychoactive cannabinoids or (semi-)synthetic cannabinoids as main active ingredients; BMI of > 27 kg/m²
